question:
A wire of length $40\ \text{cm}$ is cut into two parts. One part is bent to form a square and the other part is bent to form a circle.

(a) If $x\ \text{cm}$ is used to form the square, express the sum of the enclosed areas as a function of $x$.

(b) Determine how the wire should be divided so that the sum of the areas is minimum.

(c) Verify the minimum using the second derivative test and calculate the minimum total area.
explanation:
(a)
The side of the square is $\frac{x}{4}\ \text{cm}$, so its area is
$$A_1=\left(\frac{x}{4}\right)^2=\frac{x^2}{16}$$
The length used for the circle is $(40-x)\ \text{cm}$. If its radius is $r$, then
$$2\pi r=40-x$$
$$r=\frac{40-x}{2\pi}$$
Therefore, the area of the circle is
$$A_2=\pi r^2=\frac{(40-x)^2}{4\pi}$$
Thus, the total area is
$$A(x)=\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{(40-x)^2}{4\pi}$$

(b)
Differentiating,
$$A'(x)=\frac{x}{8}-\frac{40-x}{2\pi}$$
For a stationary value,
$$\frac{x}{8}=\frac{40-x}{2\pi}$$
$$2\pi x=8(40-x)$$
$$\pi x=4(40-x)$$
$$x(\pi+4)=160$$
Therefore,
$$x=\frac{160}{\pi+4}\ \text{cm}$$
The length used for the circle is
$$40-x=40-\frac{160}{\pi+4}=\frac{40\pi}{\pi+4}\ \text{cm}$$

(c)
The second derivative is
$$A''(x)=\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{2\pi}>0$$
Hence, the stationary value gives the minimum total area.
Substituting $x=\frac{160}{\pi+4}$,
$$A_{\min}=\frac{1}{16}\left(\frac{160}{\pi+4}\right)^2+\frac{1}{4\pi}\left(\frac{40\pi}{\pi+4}\right)^2$$
$$A_{\min}=\frac{1600}{(\pi+4)^2}+\frac{400\pi}{(\pi+4)^2}$$
$$A_{\min}=\frac{400(4+\pi)}{(\pi+4)^2}$$
Therefore,
$$A_{\min}=\frac{400}{\pi+4}\ \text{cm}^2$$

options.A:
(a) $A(x)=\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{(40-x)^2}{4\pi}$
(b) Square length $\frac{160}{\pi+4}$ cm and circle length $\frac{40\pi}{\pi+4}$ cm
(c) Minimum total area $\frac{400}{\pi+4}$ cm$^2$
options.B:
(a) $A(x)=\frac{x^2}{4}+\frac{(40-x)^2}{\pi}$
(b) Equal wire lengths $20$ cm each
(c) Minimum area $\frac{800}{\pi+4}$ cm$^2$
options.C:
(a) $A(x)=\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{(40-x)^2}{2\pi}$
(b) Square length $\frac{80}{\pi+2}$ cm
(c) Minimum area $\frac{200}{\pi+2}$ cm$^2$
options.D:
(a) $A(x)=\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{(40-x)^2}{4\pi}$
(b) Square length $\frac{40\pi}{\pi+4}$ cm and circle length $\frac{160}{\pi+4}$ cm
(c) Minimum total area $\frac{400\pi}{\pi+4}$ cm$^2$
